FINA 1303.title: Introduction to Financial Markets and Institutions
FINA 1303.description: A broad introduction to financial institutions and financial markets, providing students with an understanding of how financial systems work, the functions of various financial institutions and the role of financial regulation.
cilos: Explain and apply basic interest rate concepts in particular Discounted Cash Flow (DCF)
Calculate interest on basic financial instruments
Apply simple pricing theories such as the Dividend Discount Model (DDM)
Explain the function and organization of financial markets and institutions and the interactions between them
Explain ethical and professional responsibility of finance professionals through the discussion of current social responsibility and ethical issues in finance during class

FINA 1303.title: Introduction to Financial Markets and Institutions
FINA 1303.description: A broad introduction to financial institutions and financial markets, providing students with an understanding of how financial systems work, the functions of various financial institutions and the role of financial regulation.
cilos: Explain and apply basic interest rate concepts in particular Discounted Cash Flow (DCF)
Calculate interest on basic financial instruments
Apply simple pricing theories such as the Dividend Discount Model (DDM)
Explain the function and organization of financial markets and institutions and the interactions between them
Explain ethical and professional responsibility of finance professionals through the discussion of current social responsibility and ethical issues in finance during class

FINA 2101.title: Introduction to Finance
FINA 2101.description: For Quantitative Finance students only. The course aims to provide orientation to students to help them prepare for academic studies and understand the finance industry. The course starts with a lecture series to provide student with an overview of financial markets and institutions and raises their awareness about finance issues. It will be followed by company visits whereby students are taken to major financial institutions and corporations and meet with company representatives.
cilos: Explain the function and organization of financial markets and institutions and the interactions between them.
Understand ethical and professional responsibility of finance professionals.

FINA 2203.title: Fundamentals of Business Finance
FINA 2203.description: For BIBU and non-SB&M students. This course provides an introduction to corporate finance for students who may not have background in accounting and business statistics. Topics include financial statement analysis, time value of money, bond and stock valuation, capital budgeting, risk and return concepts and cost of capital.
cilos: Analyze firm financial performance through basic financial statement analysis.
Apply the concept of time value of money to make correct financial decisions.
Analyze the attractiveness of investment projects using various capital budgeting techniques, and understand the merits and drawbacks of each technique.
Explain the fundamental principles underlying asset valuation, and compute asset prices using a variety of approaches.
Explain the key concepts of risk, return, and diversification.
Explain the key concepts and implications of cost of capital.

FINA 2303.title: Financial Management
FINA 2303.description: For SB&M students only. This course provides an introduction to corporate finance. Topics include time value of money, bond and stock valuation, capital budgeting, risk and return concepts and cost of capital.
FINA 2303.prerequisite: ACCT 2010 AND (CIVL 2160 OR IEDA 2520 OR IEDA 2540 OR ISOM 2500 OR LIFS 3150 OR MATH 2411)
cilos: Analyze firm financial performance through basic financial statement analysis.
Apply the concept of time value of money to make correct financial decisions.
Analyze the attractiveness of investment projects using various capital budgeting techniques, and understand the merits and drawbacks of each technique.
Explain the fundamental principles underlying asset valuation, and compute asset prices using a variety of approaches.
Explain the key concepts of risk, return, and diversification.
Explain the key concepts and implications of cost of capital.

FINA 3001.title: Key Skills for Finance Professionals (A)
FINA 3001.description: The course aims to develop students' competitive edge so they are well prepared for their internships and future careers. Graded P, PP, or F. For students with major in FINA only. Students are required to complete the course within four regular terms.
cilos: Acquire in-depth knowledge and insights in current finance topics.
Acquire necessary skills to develop own professional identity.
Develop interpersonal, communication and organizational skills and build networking relationship with peers, practitioners and professionals.
Develop analytical skills, research skills, and presentation skills with actual hands-on experience.
Perform with professional and ethical code of conduct.

FINA 3001.title: Key Skills for Finance Professionals (A)
FINA 3001.description: The course aims to develop students' competitive edge so they are well prepared for their internships and future careers. Graded P, PP, or F. For students with major in FINA only. Students are required to complete the course within four regular terms.
cilos: Acquire in-depth knowledge and insights in current finance topics.
Acquire necessary skills to develop own professional identity.
Develop interpersonal, communication and organizational skills and build networking relationship with peers, practitioners and professionals.
Develop analytical skills, research skills, and presentation skills with actual hands-on experience.
Perform with professional and ethical code of conduct.

FINA 3103.title: Intermediate Investments
FINA 3103.description: This course studies the concepts and evidence relevant to the management of investment portfolios. Topics include diversification, asset allocation, portfolio optimization, factor models, the relation between risk and return, trading, passive (e.g., index-fund) and active (e.g., hedge-fund, long-short) strategies, mutual funds, performance evaluation, long-horizon investing and simulation.
cilos: Allocate capital across different asset classes based on established financial theories.
Evaluate and price financial assets using appropriate valuation models.
Assess portfolio performance to determine the effectiveness of portfolio management strategies.
Compare and contrast various investment strategies, including passive and active portfolio management.
Conduct financial analysis using quantitative tools and techniques.

FINA 3111.title: Finance Professional Development
FINA 3111.description: The course aims to provide QFIN students with increased opportunities to acquire knowledge of the finance industry, connect with professionals and peers as well as to gain hands-on experience to develop interpersonal skills. The goal is to enhance their employability and long-term career success. Additionally, the course aims to promote peer support and strengthen community bonding through participation in department/program activities. Students are required to take the course for every regular term in which they are in residency at HKUST with major in QFIN. For students with major in QFIN only. Graded P/PP/F.
cilos: Acquire a better understanding of current finance topics.
Enhance interpersonal skills through connections with professionals and peers.
Apply financial knowledge through hands-on experiences.

FINA 3203.title: Derivative Securities
FINA 3203.description: This course covers options, forward contracts, futures contracts and swaps. By the end of this course, students will have a good knowledge of how derivative contracts work, how they are used and how they are priced.
cilos: Understand the mechanics of the derivatives markets including futures, options, and swaps.
Use derivatives for hedging risks.
Use derivatives for trading views on direction and volatility.
Explain the principles of derivative pricing and analyze the impact of different factors on derivative prices.

FINA 3303.title: Intermediate Corporate Finance
FINA 3303.description: The course provides an in-depth treatment of long-term financing decisions, including estimation of the cost of capital, financial leverage, corporate distress, raising financing, dividend policy, and working capital analysis.
cilos: Apply finance theories to explain how firms choose their capital structure.
Value projects and firms using various valuation models, including discounted cash flow and relative valuation techniques.
Understand how firms raise capital and compute the cost of financing for various alternatives.
Understand payout policy, including dividends and share repurchases, and how factors such as taxes influence corporate decisions.
Understand how firms manage net working capital and analyze their effectiveness in doing so.

FINA 3810.title: Bloomberg Market Concepts Certification
FINA 3810.description: The course aims to provide students with knowledge of financial markets and Bloomberg functionality. The course consists of four modules: economic indicators, currencies, fixed income and equities. Students will need to complete all four modules to receive the Bloomberg Market Concepts certification. Graded P or F. For students with major in FINA, QFIN and SGFN only.
cilos: Use Bloomberg data, news, and tools to explain developments in global equity, fixed income, and currency markets.
Explain how key economic indicators are published and used in market analysis.
Navigate Bloomberg Terminal functionality to locate key financial data.

FINA 3810.title: Bloomberg Market Concepts Certification
FINA 3810.description: The course aims to provide students with knowledge of financial markets and Bloomberg functionality. The course consists of four modules: economic indicators, currencies, fixed income and equities. Students will need to complete all four modules to receive the Bloomberg Market Concepts certification. Graded P or F. For students with major in FINA, QFIN and SGFN only.
cilos: Use Bloomberg data, news, and tools to explain developments in global equity, fixed income, and currency markets.
Explain how key economic indicators are published and used in market analysis.
Navigate Bloomberg Terminal functionality to locate key financial data.

FINA 3820.title: Refinitiv Certification Program
FINA 3820.description: This course will enable students to learn more about market information and the functionality of a Refinitiv data product most commonly used by financial professionals. It begins with the first module of basic overview and is followed by four core modules on data, screen design, graphics, analysis tools of various instruments, which includes one module of data retrieval in Excel. Students will be eligible in attending the Refinitiv Certification Assessment upon completion of the course. Graded P or F.
cilos: Use LSEG Workspace to access and interpret financial data, market-leading Reuters news, and analytics.
Apply LSEG Workspace tools and content to support informed financial decision-making.

FINA 3830.title: Bloomberg, LSEG with Artificial Intelligence Tools
FINA 3830.description: This course provides students with a hands‑on, experiential introduction to professional financial data platforms and emerging AI technologies that are transforming the investment and analytics landscape. Students will develop practical skills using Bloomberg Terminal, London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) Workspace, and a range of artificial intelligence tools commonly applied in investment analysis. Graded P or F.
cilos: Effectively navigate and retrieve financial market data using Bloomberg Terminal and LSEG Workspace across major asset classes and key macroeconomic indicators.
Apply AI enabled analytics tools to support financial modelling, data analysis, and investment research.
Integrate professional data platforms with human judgment to construct dashboards, research summaries, and coherent investment storylines.

FINA 3830.title: Refinitiv Analytics
FINA 3830.description: The objective of the course is to give students first hand experience in using Refinitiv terminals and provide them with a firm foundation of analytical skills and practical market knowledge. Graded P or F.
cilos: Use LSEG Workspace analytical tools to generate and support investment ideas.
Implement Python-based workflows powered by LSEG APIs and data analytics.

FINA 4003.title: Wealth Management
FINA 4003.description: This course focuses on a broad understanding of financial and investment issues arising in the context of personal wealth management. Students will gain an understanding of the nature and use of various financial products and legal instruments for developing a financial plan. It covers topics such as client financial status and expectations, portfolio management, securities trading, managed funds, insurance, and tax and estate planning.
cilos: Implement the financial planning process while following the professional practices.
Apply personal profiling and risk profiling techniques to comprehend the unique situation and preferences of the client.
Prioritize goals and determine the feasibility of achieving these goals.
Construct personal financial statements and use ratios and other techniques to analyze the client’s financial situation.
Demonstrate the ability to develop and justify the economic assumptions used in a financial plan.
Construct optimal portfolios and make asset allocation decisions which match goals, risk tolerance and other client characteristics using Morningstar Direct.

Demonstrate the ability to analyze, synthesize, and evaluate personal financial situations, and implement goal funding strategies by determining realistic targets and conducting capital needs analysis for retirement and other financial objectives.
Demonstrate the ability to clearly discuss and justify recommendations.

FINA 4013.title: Corporate Valuation
FINA 4013.description: This course teaches students how to use financial information to value firms. By the end of this course, students will be able to value firms using discounted cash flow valuation, relative valuation, and real options.
cilos: Analyze firm financial performance using financial statements to identify key value drivers.
Develop projected financial statements and forecast free cash flows for valuation purposes.
Estimate the cost of capital.
Apply discounted cash flow (DCF) models to value firms and conduct sensitivity analysis.
Use relative valuation techniques and other valuation methods to complement DCF analysis.
Apply valuation models to real world situations.

FINA 4103.title: Financial Markets Trading and Structure
FINA 4103.description: This course examines liquidity, market structure and trading. The focus is on examining the efficiency of trading systems and markets, the impact of new algorithmic trading on markets, the role of intermediaries and regulatory actions on market structure issues. Students learn about a number of alternative market structures in terms of their economic and operational effectiveness.
cilos: Comprehend how to incorporate the notion of "information" in analyses of financial market.
Theoretically and empirically measure market liquidity.
Understand various financial market details and trading structures.
Understand the impact of recent development of financial technologies.
Analyze market quality in various situations with different market structures, trading rules, and market policies.

FINA 4203.title: Mergers, Acquisitions, and Corporate Restructuring
FINA 4203.description: This course analyzes mechanisms underlying the creation of value in mergers, acquisitions and corporate restructuring. Students will learn analytical techniques and tools to analyze (a) strategy behind corporate restructuring transactions, whether and what to acquire, (b) evaluation and financing of acquisitions, and (c) decisions and processes that impact value creation in mergers.
cilos: Apply valuation techniques in M&A settings.
Analyze how M&A deals are financed and structured.
Evaluate the mechanisms and effectiveness of anti-takeover defenses.
Explain corporate restructurings, including divestitures and spinoffs.
Assess the role and impact of corporate governance in M&A transactions.

FINA 4303.title: Fixed Income Securities
FINA 4303.description: Pricing of bonds, term structure models, duration analysis and immunization techniques, valuation of interest rate options, convertible bonds, mortgage-backed securities, pricing credit derivatives, bond portfolio construction and management.
cilos: Evaluate and price a wide range of fixed income instruments—including traditional and structured bonds—using appropriate financial models and analytical tools.
Analyze interest rate risk using measures such as duration and convexity, and apply yield curve construction techniques including bootstrapping.
Design and assess fixed income portfolio management strategies, including immunization and hedging approaches, in the context of changing market conditions.
Understand and apply the mechanics and valuation of interest rate derivatives such as swaps, futures, and credit derivatives.
Evaluate emerging trends and innovations in fixed income markets, and assess their implications for investment strategies and risk management.

FINA 4403.title: International Finance
FINA 4403.description: An introduction to the fundamental principles of international financial management and investment.  Topics include: international financial markets and instruments; foreign exchange markets; foreign currency derivatives and currency risk; international capital budgeting; international bond and equity markets.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of the international dimensions of financial markets, including the international monetary system, capital markets, regulatory frameworks, risk factors, and investor behavior.
Apply finance concepts and theories to evaluate and make informed decisions in international business and investment contexts.
Apply economic principles to explain the determinants and dynamics of exchange rate movements.
Discuss how to use derivatives such as futures, options, and swaps to manage risks faced by multinational corporations.
Explain the principles of international portfolio management, including the relationship between risk and return across individual assets and investment portfolios.
Describe and explain recent developments related to financial markets outside Hong Kong.

FINA 4413.title: Family Business
FINA 4413.description: This course aims to provide students with comprehensive and practical understanding of Asian family business, which is the most prominent and significant business form in Asia. The course will specifically cover valuation and ownership design, financing and exit strategies, governance and succession practices of family businesses. The course is application oriented and draws on the faculty’s research experience and active interactions with family businesses in Asia. This course will benefit not only the students who will work in family businesses but also those likely to provide services to them in the future, such as private and investment bankers, family office professionals, private equity professionals, and other service professionals working closely with wealthy families in the region.
cilos: Understand the fundamentals of family business including its definition, importance, complexity, and how it differs from non-family business.
Analyse the factors contributing to the longevity of family businesses, and the causes for the potential early demise.
Understand the financing options of family business, and risk related to getting listed and over-borrowing.
Valuate the family business for different purposes, including pruning of ownership, professionalizing of family business and selling of family business.
Prepare for Leadership and ownership succession planning.
Design suitable structures and governance systems for wealth creators to preserve family wealth, legacy, and harmony across generations.

FINA 4423.title: Family Office
FINA 4423.description: This course provides students with a comprehensive and most up-to-date understanding of family office, as well as insiders’ view and practical aspects of family office. For university students who are about to graduate and are interested in entering into family office related sectors, having an in-depth understanding of family office will definitely help them better prepared for the future.
cilos: Understand the fundamentals of family business and the factors contributing to the longevity of family businesses.
Prepare for leadership and ownership succession.
Understand the need for transition from family business to family office.
Understand the fundamentals of family office, single family office vs multi family office.
Understand the definition and measurements of impact investments and be able to engage it practically.
Understand the different approaches and impacts of family philanthropy.
Design a suitable family governance structure.
Understand art collection and investment of family office.

FINA 4503.title: Banking and Financial Intermediation
FINA 4503.description: This course examines financial intermediaries with a particular emphasis on banks. It introduces students to the nature, purpose, and management of these institutions. The course also brings together the upstream issues in risk measurement and the regulative environment surrounding banks. By the end of this course, students will be able to understand the role of banks in the economy and the effects of frictions such as information asymmetry and agency costs on bank behavior. The course will start with the review of basic game theory.
cilos: Explain why financial intermediaries exist in the economy and understand how they create value.
Explain informational frictions and agency costs in bank lending behavior.
Describe the risks banks take in their operations.
Understand the need and nature of bank regulations.

FINA 4513.title: Risk Management
FINA 4513.description: This course covers the role of risk management in supporting companies as they strive to balance the internal and external risk factors surrounding the operation of their business model against their various stakeholder obligations. Topics include a review of basic hedging strategies (knowledge of futures and options is pre-requisite), the theory and evidence on the value of corporate risk management, review of major surveys of risk management practices, business-case studies highlighting advanced derivatives and risk-management strategies, an illustrative model of integrated enterprise risk- management (featuring Monte-Carlo simulation), and student-led risk-management audits.
cilos: Understand how to identify, measure, and assess risks.
Design and implement advanced derivatives and hedging strategies to preserve and add value.
Analyze and evaluate risk factors by modeling their causes and effects through enterprise risk management frameworks.
Apply the risk management concepts and tools to various cases and scenarios.

FINA 4603.title: Venture Capital Financing
FINA 4603.description: This course covers the application of financial tools and techniques to the funding and valuation of an entrepreneurial venture. The course seeks to provide students with a background on the venture capital industry, the economic intuition underlying its features, and the basic tools required to work in the industry.
cilos: Understand the structure and key players of the venture capital industry.
Understand how venture capitalists identify, add, and capture value in portfolio companies.
Evaluate the incentives and roles of different stakeholders in the venture capital ecosystem.
Understand and assess the types of contracts used in VC deals, and how they influence control, risk, and returns.
Assess and value exit strategies, including IPOs, acquisitions, and secondary sales.

FINA 4703.title: ESG Investing
FINA 4703.description: This course focuses on the relevance of sustainability factors on financial performance of firms and securities. Topics in this course include the market terminology, practices, usages and impact of environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors and climate risk. Students will learn to analyze complex financial problems, adapt investment strategies to meet business needs, propose solutions that maximize stakeholder value, and apply ESG related concepts to the process of investment management and valuation.
cilos: Understand the definition and importance of ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance).
Understand the tradeoff between financial and social returns.
Describe the trends in the asset management industry and impact investing.
Identify the channels through which impact investing improves sustainability.
Explain the relationship between ESG, impact investing, and firms’ performance.

FINA 4713.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence and Big Data in Finance
FINA 4713.description: This course provides an overview of the main branches of AI and Big Data, and exposes students to real-world industry use cases to help them understand the impact that AI will have on the finance industry. Upon completion of this course, students will be able to identify and leverage AI and Big Data to enhance and/or disrupt business models, while keeping in mind social and ethical considerations.
cilos: Understand the fundamental branches of Artificial Intelligence and Big Data.
Gain insight into the use cases of AI/Big Data within Finance and the Financial Markets.
Critically evaluate use cases of AI/Big Data from the perspective of data, technology, human capital and change management.
Identify concerns relating to the AI/Big Data from a regulatory, organizational, societal and personal standpoint.
Anticipate the future evolutions and potential ethical issues surrounding the impact of AI/Big Data.

FINA 4723.title: Responsible Finance
FINA 4723.description: This course is designed to give students a thorough overview of responsible finance and ESG. The first part covers fundamental topics related to ESG. The second part focuses more on project and firm valuation with an ESG perspective. It also covers financial models that will allow one to understand how to incorporate ESG factors in financial decisions.
cilos: Identify and explain the driving forces of responsible finance.
Understand the objective of corporation.
Understand how investors can engage with firms in effective manners.
Apply tools and data sets to evaluate ESG performance.
Analyze corporate projects using ESG criteria.
Evaluate firm performance using ESG methods.

FINA 4803.title: Quantitative Trading
FINA 4803.description: For QFIN students in their fourth year of study only. This is a capstone course for final year students in the BSc Quantitative Finance program. Working in groups, the students will bring together all the knowledge learned in the program to develop and execute a quantitative trading strategy through a simulated platform. The instructor will guide the students through the following stages: (1) idea generation, (2) strategy backtesting, (3) risk management planning, (4) system development, (5) trade execution, and (6) performance evaluation. Students will also have the opportunity to develop their leadership and presentation skills.
cilos: Develop a quantitative trading strategy.
Develop a risk management overlay.
Execute a trading strategy effectively.
Evaluate a trading strategy's performance.
Present a trading strategy in a professional manner.

FINA 4919.title: Independent Study
FINA 4919.description: Directed study of selected issues in Finance. May be graded by letter, or P/F for different offerings. Instructor's approval is required for enrollment in the course. Subject to approval by the department, students may repeat the course once if a different topic is selected.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of finance topics through independent research and literature review.
Apply appropriate data collection and analysis techniques to investigate a finance-related research question.
Generate insights and support evidence-based conclusions.
Communicate research findings clearly and professionally through written reports and/or oral presentations.

FINA 4929.title: Special Topics in Finance
FINA 4929.description: Covers current developments in finance. Topics selected by instructors.  May be graded P or F.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of key concepts, frameworks, or practices relevant to the course topic.
Analyze issues related to the course content using appropriate reasoning, frameworks, or tools.
Interpret and evaluate case studies, scenarios, or other relevant materials using critical thinking and appropriate analytical reasoning.

FINA 5110.title: Central Bank Operations
FINA 5110.description: This course is designed for students who intend to work in the finance industry as economists or strategists (e.g. rates strategist), both on the sell-side or the buy-side. This course starts from the fundamentals of central banks, particularly the balance sheet and relates it to central bank operations and the money creation process. The course will deep dive the Federal Reserve, covering both traditional and non-conventional policy tools. By incorporating macroeconomic diagnostics, students are encouraged to put themselves in the shoes of policymakers and predict policy decisions. This course will also study the monetary policy transmission mechanism and the link between financial and real sectors. In addition, this course links policy decisions to the pricing of assets, such as rates. The core principle of this course is “Learning by Doing”: students will be given plenty of opportunities to conduct data analysis to study the monetary policy impact to financial markets and real economy.
cilos: Read and interpret central bank balance sheets.
Recognize central bank tools, decision making process and communication.
Diagnose current macroeconomic environment.
Assess the impact of central bank policy on the financial markets and the real economy.
Understand the fundamentals of treasury securities and rates pricing.

FINA 5120.title: Corporate Finance
FINA 5120.description: Valuation of cash flow streams (PV of cash flow streams, annuities, and perpetuities); valuation of bonds; valuation of stocks using dividend discount model; capital budgeting decisions (NPV, IRR, payback); capital structure; limits to the use of debt (trade-off models); estimation of cost of debt and equity; WACC; terminal value.
cilos: Identify and analyze the objective of the firm.
Apply the concept of time value of money and discounting cash flows to situations when the cash flows and the discount rate is known.

Analyze the pros and cons of the common methods used in firms to evaluate and pick investment projects, and explain why the net present value (NPV) rule is the only one that is consistent with maximizing firm value.
Define the principles for identifying the cash flows that need to be discounted to calculate the NPV of a project.
Calculate the weighed average cost of capital and apply this to a real company.
Apply the above tools to cases that involve deciding whether to take a project and to merger decisions.

FINA 5130.title: Corporate Governance for Value Creation
FINA 5130.description: Corporate governance (CG) is about shaping incentives. CG examines how corporations induce their managers to maximize shareholder value through incentives and oversight systems (monitoring). This course examines how good corporate governance can mitigate incentive and information problems, nurture great leaders, and foster great companies. Through numerous cases and examples, we also show how bad governance can worsen these problems, lead managers to cheat, and cause companies to fall.
cilos: Describe the governance challenges facing companies and the tools of corporate governance (CG).
Explain how and why poor (good) CG destroys (creates) shareholder value.
Explain how and why the interests of various stakeholders and monitors converge or diverge.
Illustrate CG problems and solutions by drawing on a large set of illustrative cases and examples.
Critically read a CG report to assess the strengths and weaknesses of a company’s CG.
Propose a structured CG audit of a company or a situation based on sound economic principles.
Interpret the results of such an audit and make well-reasoned recommendations for improvement.
Professionally communicate audit results, interpretation, recommendations, in writing and orally.

FINA 5140.title: Advanced Topics in Financial Management
FINA 5140.description: Valuation of projects (advanced capital budgeting); estimating cost of capital; risk assessment of projects; decision tree analysis; real option valuation of projects; warrants and convertibles; leasing; dividend policy.
cilos: Solve real world finance problems that are often encountered by corporate financial managers, bankers, and asset managers.
Work effectively in a team with people from different background.
Design financial strategy and present findings, insights, and advices in an accurate manner to future clients in the financial industry.

FINA 5150.title: Corporate Risk Management
FINA 5150.description: Practical and theoretical issues in risk management from the corporate end-user's perspective; benefits and optimal strategies of risk management; current cases which have been debated in the media.
cilos: Describe the risks facing companies and the tools of corporate risk management (CRM).
Explain and illustrate the main theories relating corporate risk management to firm value.
Summarize the main empirical and survey results on the practice of corporate risk management.
Master the case studies covered and relate them to decision-making in today’s risk environment.
Conduct a structured CRM audit and make well-reasoned recommendations for improvement.

FINA 5190.title: Family Business
FINA 5190.description: This course is tailored for individuals who are currently working in or are contemplating to work in a family business, either as a family member or a non-family executive. The material covered also gives greater understanding of the dynamics of family business for current or future private and investment bankers, family office professionals, accountants, lawyers and other service professionals working closely with families of wealth in the region.
cilos: Summarize the fundamentals of family business including its definition, importance, complexity, and how it differs from non-family business.
Analyze the factors contributing to the longevity of family businesses, and the causes for the potential early demise, especially for ethnic Chinese family businesses.
Design suitable wealth management strategies, structure and governance systems for wealth creators to preserve family wealth, family legacy, and harmony across generations.
Prepare future leaders of family businesses.
Identify the similarities of and differences between Chinese family businesses and those from other ethnic groups around the world.

FINA 5210.title: Investment Analysis
FINA 5210.description: An introduction to fundamental concepts in investment analysis. The first part covers risk and return tradeoff, portfolio diversification, and modern portfolio theory including the capital asset pricing model and arbitrage pricing theory. The second part covers basic analytical tools used in analyzing fixed income securities. Topics include interest rates and yield curve mathematics, duration and convexity.
cilos: Apply Utility theory in finance, identifying the risk-return tradeoff, and derive the ‘correct’ price for financial assets using models such as the CAPM.
Practically apply CAPM and other models (e.g. Fama-French 3 factor model) in Excel-based applications.
Explain efficient markets, behavioral finance, and some trading strategies based on perceived violations of efficient market theory.

FINA 5220.title: Equity Investment Management
FINA 5220.description: The course covers the complete investment process including: constructing investment objectives, outlining investment policies; choosing asset allocations; monitoring investments; and measuring performance.  Practical issues relating to investment style, active management, and passive management are discussed. Advanced techniques in portfolio construction such as the Black-Litterman model and multi-factor models are studied.
cilos: Apply the concepts of diversification, and adopt risk hedging, and optimal portfolio model to search for an optimal risk-return profile for a risky portfolio.
Apply multi-factor risk model in active equity investment management.
Analyze the effect of asymmetric information and liquidity on equity portfolio.

FINA 5230.title: ESG Investing
FINA 5230.description: This course puts together a collection of industry cases, projects and academic papers on Sustainable Investing, also known as ESG Investing. It is an investment approach that integrates three additional factors - environment (E), social (S) and governance (G), into security analysis and portfolio allocation. As the industry successfully adopts these factors into their double bottom line financial analysis, only a handful of courses - such as this one - would tackle the subject. This course will discuss the market terminology, practices, usages and dollar impact of ESG factors. The main focus is on the identification, measurement and the materiality of ESG indicators. The students will learn that financial analysis with ESG integration provides the basis for a more informed investment decision. Discussion on existing academic papers will shed light on the cost and benefits of sustainable investing. This course will empower the students with cutting edge information, tools and solid research on the subject.
cilos: Analyze and comment on complex real-world financial problems.
Adapt investment strategies to meet business needs.
Propose asset/risk-management solutions that maximize stakeholder value.
Apply the principles, skills, methods, techniques, and knowledge of modern finance to the process of investment management and securities valuation.

FINA 5240.title: FinTech Analytics
FINA 5240.description: The course will be based on the open-source Python language which provides a wide variety of statistical and graphical techniques, and is well-suited for data manipulation, calculation and graphical display. The first part of the course will be for general introduction to Python, and then use of specific tools like matrix manipulation, optimization, random numbers and simulation, etc. will be illustrated with financial applications. Some familiarity and prior experience with a proper programming language, beyond standard Excel, is recommended.
cilos: Demonstrate functional proficiency in Python programming.
Apply the control and data structures to solve computational problems.
Perform data input/output and simulations, and produce high quality graphics/plots.
Use packages of relevance to quantitative finance.
Apply the programming techniques in financial context.

FINA 5250.title: Empirical Methods in Finance
FINA 5250.description: This course studies the techniques of empirical investigation in finance. Students are introduced to recent empirical findings based on asset pricing and corporate finance models. The course includes a selection of econometrics topics and their finance applications. Students will apply the techniques using a programming language.
cilos: Apply econometric techniques for financial data analysis.
Analyze important facts and puzzles in asset pricing and corporate finance.
Use R programming language for data analysis.

FINA 5260.title: FinTech: The Future of the Financial Industry
FINA 5260.description: This is an introductory course to Financial Technology (FinTech) which includes Insurance Technology (InsurTech) and Regulation Technology (RegTech). The student will have a solid understanding of the underlying information technology being applied in various innovative business models to disrupt the finance and banking landscape globally. The critical business, social/ethical, legal and technology issues and the related risks faced by corporate executives when planning FinTech projects using quant finance models, DLT, crypto-token, AI, big data and algorithms to drive innovations in banking and finance will be discussed in class. Live demos will be conducted to illustrate the proof-of-concept and their applications in real world scenarios.  Key industry developments and the impact to stakeholders will be examined.
cilos: Identify the FinTech, InsurTech and RegTech landscape, its segment, regulations and ecosystem.
Confidently drive FinTech project developments as part of the executive team and deal with arising issues from various stakeholders, i.e. IT, legal, audit, compliance and regulations.

FINA 5270.title: Portfolio Management with Fintech Applications
FINA 5270.description: This course will focus on the key dimensions of Portfolio Management with FinTech Applications, and will give a predominant place to Artificial Intelligence, as a way to process and leverage the “Big Data” and automate the Portfolio and Wealth Management processes. The course will begin by a brief review of the fundamentals of Portfolio Management, FinTech and Artificial Intelligence and the advances in technology and data that has led the industry to where it is today. It will then delve into the Asset Management and Wealth Management value chains through a series of applications that enable students the critical skills they need to operate as expert actors in FinTech. The course will also expose students to the existing FinTech landscape and ecosystem within the portfolio management industry and will also touch upon on how Artificial Intelligence augments humans to make them better portfolio and wealth managers.
cilos: Explain the fundamentals of portfolio management with FinTech applications.
Recognize the FinTech landscape within the Portfolio Management space.
Use Artificial Intelligence in Portfolio Management to solve applied Business Problems.
Present the future trends that are coming to Portfolio Management.

FINA 5280.title: Smart Applications of Distributed Ledger Technology
FINA 5280.description: Blockchain and Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) are growing in use. This course covers the fundamental concept, design and implementation of the distributed ledgers and blockchain technologies in FinTech, InsurTech and other business areas. The characteristics and properties, as well as misconceptions, of blockchains will be discussed.
cilos: Understand what is Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) / Blockchain that supports the disruptive business strategies/models in banking and finance.
Explore and critically examine the deployment of any one or more of the DLTs, i.e. Blockchain, Ethereum, Hyperledger, R3 Corda and Stella in different environments.
Design the FinTech/InsurTech/RegTech business using BIDT and LoNG PESTEL model.
Analyze the socio-economic impact in the deployment of DLT instead of the traditional model.
Acquire the fundamental and practical knowledge to be entrepreneur or project management in the FinTech and Innovation industry.

FINA 5290.title: Derivatives Analysis
FINA 5290.description: Basic characteristics of derivatives instruments such as forwards, futures, options, and swaps. Topics include pricing of futures and forward contracts, forward-spot basis risk, option strategies, put-call parity and introduction to the Black-Scholes model. The development and use of interest rate and currency swaps are also discussed.
cilos: Define the mechanics of the derivatives markets including futures, options and swaps.
Use derivatives for hedging risks.
Use derivatives for trading various views on direction and volatility.
Explain price derivatives and how prices change with respect to different factors.

FINA 5330.title: Investment and Finance in China and Asia
FINA 5330.description: This course provides a practical understanding of foreign investment in China and Asia, and how financing is used for trade and investment in the region. Students will be able to develop ability to successfully complete deals in China and other Asian markets through taking this course.
cilos: To compare different kinds of financial structures in the Chinese and Asian contexts.
To analyze new situations to identify which techniques and contextual factors are the most critical.
To design and implement strategies using financial techniques in order to structure, negotiate and close deals in a variety of Chinese and Asian contexts.

FINA 5360.title: Fixed Income Analysis
FINA 5360.description: Includes techniques in fixed-income portfolio management and introduction of fixed-income derivatives. Topics include term-structure theories, yield-curve fitting techniques and yield curve trading strategies, portfolio performance evaluation, floating rate securities, forward rate agreements, bond and interest rate futures, and interest rate swaps.
cilos: Identify basic valuation techniques of the traditional fixed-income securities, based on concepts such as price-yield relationship, alternative definitions of yields, price sensitivity measures (durations and convexities).
Calculate spot rates, discount factors, forward rates, par-bond yields, holding period returns, and identify classical theories of the term structure of interest rate.
Implement yield-curve fitting techniques and some simple portfolio strategies.
Recognize more advanced concepts like repos and floating rate, and develop the necessary economic intuition and quantitative skills.

FINA 5370.title: Equity Valuation
FINA 5370.description: Basic valuation approaches including dividend discount model, free cash flows model, and valuation by multiples; measures of company performance and value added; valuation in special situations such as emerging markets, closely held companies, mergers, and divestitures.
cilos: Use standard equity valuation models, like discounted cash flow (DCF) , to assess the value of a firm or a project.
Understand the value driving factors, for example, management team, market monopolistic power, and technological barrier, from the angle of a private equity manager.
Understand the difference in the equity pricing/valuation practice between the western world and the Greater China region.
Use certain models to detect the potential frauds in financial statements.
Use real options in assessing the value of firm or project when facing high uncertainty.

FINA 5390.title: Venture Capital and Private Equity
FINA 5390.description: Topics include: (1) An overview of the venture capital and private equity markets in Asia; (2) Deal structuring; (3) Valuation techniques; (4) Due diligence and post-investment management; (5) Understanding the terms in term sheets; (6) Negotiating term sheets; (7) Going public, trade sale and other exit strategies.  Real-world examples from throughout Asia will be used to illustrate these topics.
cilos: Explain the world of VCPE investments.
Analyze challenges associated with each cycle of the VCPE process from pre-investment to post-investment.

Implement VCPE key screening criteria to identify and screen prospective investee companies, and develop skills and understanding necessary to perform VCPE due diligence for prospective investee firms.
Evaluate term sheet structure, key terms and understand their limitations and challenges.
Apply VCPE fund governance, management, and return measures in practice.

Apply valuation techniques to value private firms, including market, income, and asset-based approaches, and describe practical limitations of various valuation techniques and the importance of understanding assumptions of the underlying business valuations.
Administer the highly practical approach to mitigating, adjusting VCPE risks.
Draft investment memo to address investment rationale, risks, and rewards in practice.
Evaluate routes of VCPE exits, including trade sale, secondary buyout, IPO, among others.

“Experience” the realm of being a VCPE professional by engaging in a “hackathon” way of negotiation between the buyer (VCPE) and the seller (investee firm) that aims to mimic the real world environment.

FINA 5410.title: Market Microstructure
FINA 5410.description: The course is designed to provide students with an overview of how supply equals demand in real-world financial markets. After taking this course , students would be able to appreciate the frictions existing in actual financial markets - bid-ask spreads, trade impact on price, brokerage commissions, quantity limitations, time delays, market manipulation, etc. - and be able to devise trading strategies that minimize these frictions.
cilos: Broaden and deepen their understanding of finance, explain how financial markets actually work and minimize trading costs when they trade for themselves or their employers.
Apply practical skills to explain real-time quotes and analyze the costs of trading.
Demonstrate effective communication in oral English through group presentations.
Develop creative and critical thinking through the group project of developing their original trading strategy or analysis of a brewing trading controversy.
Work effectively in multi-cultural settings.
Recognize ethical and professional responsibility of finance professionals; in particular through the discussions of the dark side of trading.

FINA 5440.title: Risk Management for Financial Institutions
FINA 5440.description: Brief overview of financial intermediaries and their functions.  Measures of interest rate risk: periodic (re-pricing) gap, duration gap.  Management of interest rate risk using appropriate composition of assets and liabilities, futures, options, caps, floors, collars, swaps.  Market risk: value at risk measures.  Management of credit risk, off-balance sheet risk, liquidity risk, capital adequacy.  Deposit insurance.  With selected case studies.
cilos: Understand how a bank organizes itself to manage different types of risks.
Critically review structures and proposals to identify key risks and think about potential mitigants.
Understand the latest concepts in risk management.

FINA 5450.title: Hedge Funds
FINA 5450.description: Alternative investments are the fastest growing sector of the financial industry, and probably the least understood, including by several market professionals.  Although the range of sophistication in people associated with alternative investments varies substantially, it is more and more common to use them in investment strategies, either as direct investments or through funds of funds or structured products.  The purpose of this course is to give participants a good understanding and workable knowledge of the techniques that should be part of the tool kit of anyone investing in, analyzing and/or advising private and institutional clients on the inclusion of alternative investments - and more specifically hedge funds - in their portfolios.  Furthermore, this course will enable the participants to absorb the analytical arguments in the technical publications - the in-house research notes of financial institutions and in practitioner oriented journal - that deal with alternative investments and to apply them.
cilos: Understand what hedge funds are and how they are structured.
Understand the major hedge fund strategies, their potential risks and expected rewards.
Understand how to analyze hedge funds qualitatively and quantitatively.

FINA 5470.title: Mergers, Acquisitions and Restructuring
FINA 5470.description: Focuses on the design, analysis, and implementation of financial strategies aimed at repositioning and revitalizing companies.  Corporate value creation by restructuring a company or by undergoing a business combination.
cilos: Measure the value created by M&A/Restructuring.
Evaluate the tactics and the effect of management opposition to M&A.
Understand the role of Private Equity, activists/raiders in corporate restructuring.
Implement merger arbitrage tactics.
Understand the role of corporate governance in M&A/Restructuring decisions.

FINA 5480.title: Commodities, Trade Finance and Infrastructures
FINA 5480.description: This course will focus on three alternative "asset classes", namely commodities, trade finance and infrastructures. The purpose of this course is to give participants a good understanding and workable knowledge of the techniques that should be part of the toolkit of anyone investing in, trading, hedging, analyzing and/or advising private and institutional clients on these three alternative asset classes. Furthermore, this course will enable the participants to absorb the analytical arguments in the technical publications – the in-house research notes of financial institutions and in practitioner oriented journals – that deal with commodities and their markets, and to apply them.
cilos: Identify and explain the types and nature of commodities in general, their pricing mechanisms and the methods by which these commodities are traded.
Implement commodity trades and size them appropriately.
Explain the contractual principles underpinning trade finance.
Describe and explain infrastructure investing.
Present a research topic about these alternative investments.

FINA 5490.title: Advanced Venture Capital Investing
FINA 5490.description: This course is a follow-up of FINA 5390 Venture Capital and Private Equity, with a particular focus on early-stage venture companies. Students will be able to experience and practice all the learned materials, particularly those related to the venture capital (VC) endeavors, in real-world VC settings. Students will “invest” alongside VC practitioners as well as being guided by them on various topics such as screening prospective investee companies in a live pitch session and drafting and compiling due diligence lists, term sheets, the required closing documentations, and valuation assessments, in addition to presenting early-read memos to industry professionals (e.g., members of the investment committee (IC)) for deal approvals, among other topics. The professor will frequently relate concepts discussed in class to transactions currently in the news to illustrate their application and limitations.
cilos: Use venture capital (VC) investing fundamentals in the real world.
Interact with investee companies.
Select investee companies and enhance themselves using advanced evaluation matrices.
Generate due diligence list and explain the rationale behind it.
Conduct due diligence on investee companies and explain how Investment Committee (IC) members approve investment deals.

Value investee companies using methods recommended by International Private Equity Valuation
Guidelines (IPEVG), including option pricing.
Negotiate term sheets and explore deal structures with investee companies.
Close deals (or not) with investee companies, draft closing reports, and conduct post-deal analyses.

FINA 5500.title: VC Entrepreneurships
FINA 5500.description: This course will cover how the Venture Capital (VC) industry works, all the parties involved, and the dynamics therein. By illustrating real world examples in some of the largest and most respected and successful VC firms in the world, students will learn how VCs raise money, how they construct a fund portfolio, how they make investment decisions, how VC returns are calculated, and how to land a job in this mysterious sector of high finance.
cilos: Understand the latest industry best practices to launch and manage a VC fund
Construct a VC fund portfolio
Decide the most appropriate valuation method for a startup
Conduct a due diligence process on a startup company
Construct a best-practice term sheet that reflects considerations to all parties
Determine the most appropriate exit strategy for an investment
Answer the question: is venture capital the right career choice for me?

FINA 5510.title: Decision Making in Financial Institutions
FINA 5510.description: In this course, students will be able to examine the nature of main financial institutions (i.e., banks, insurance companies, mutual funds, and hedge funds) as well as the incentives of decision makers in these institutions. The course also covers the purpose of bank regulation and financial crises.
cilos: Examine the nature of main financial institutions (i.e., banks, insurance companies, mutual funds, and hedge funds)
Examine the incentives of decision makers in main financial institutions
Understand the role of main financial institutions in the economy
Understand the effects of informational problems in main financial institutions
Understand the effects of agency costs on behavior of agents in main financial institutions
Critically evaluate the incentives of different economic actors in development of financial crises

FINA 5520.title: Financial Data Analysis
FINA 5520.description: Headline financial data are informative but not fully revealing, concealing hidden gems and traps. This course applies a wise-investor perspective to looking behind the scenes of financial statements. Building from the ground up, students learn how to spot abnormalities, develop pro-forma financials, build solid valuation models, and gain the knowledge and skills to pitch sound investment strategies. These foundations are supplemented by several real-world study cases illustrating accounting issues such as revenue recognition, valuation, and failed unicorns.
cilos: Explain the connections between the financial statements.
Demonstrate key accounting concepts such as cash vs. accruals, revenue recognition, and cost structure.
Build pro-forma financials and convert them to discounted cash flow projections.
Cite relevant case studies to show how and why appealing investments can go wrong.
Integrate micro-foundations, macro-conditions, and market sentiment in formulating an investment case.
Compare and contrast the pros and cons of various valuation methods.

FINA 5530.title: Green Finance: Markets and Institutions
FINA 5530.description:
Overview of the major issues in green finance pertaining to markets and financial institutions from the standpoint of both investors and policymakers. One of the main references is a report by the Network for Greening the Financial System. Topics: 
taxonomies and green classification frameworks, green external review, climate transition metrics, disclosure requirements, green rating systems, the role  of technology in green data collection and market transparency, green product adaptations, challenges specific to China and Asia, and preparation for ESG certifications.
cilos: Trace the history of green finance, situate its current state, and project likely future trajectories.
Differentiate among financial instruments, green and traditional, and critique their shortcomings.
Review the changing disclosure environment and the reliability of key carbon emissions disclosure items.
Describe and critique the various institutions and methods for green certification and verification.
Describe the rating harmonization challenges and the role of technology in green data collection.
Narrate the green experience in emerging Asia and Japan and the case of China in particular.

FINA 5540.title: Alternative Investment Management
FINA 5540.description: This course aims to provide students a holistic introduction to the alternative investment ecosystem, covering sectors such as private equity, real estate, infrastructure, credit, hedge funds, secondaries, and others.
cilos: Describe the overall Alternative Investment (AI) ecosystem, including the various market participants and investment strategies.
Develop an Investment Policy Statement from the perspective of the different Asset Owners.
Compare and contrast across the different AI strategies in terms of the relative risk and return profiles, strengths and weaknesses, and relevance for different market participants.
Describe the different methods for accessing, evaluating, and selecting different AI strategies and investment opportunities.
Develop, prepare, and present marketing materials for different investment strategy and products.

FINA 5550.title: Carbon Management Basics for Financial Institutions
FINA 5550.description: The world needs to reach net zero emission by 2050 to keep global warming within 1.5 °C by the end of this century. Financial sector plays an important role in this net zero transition. This course equips the students with the basic knowledge and practical tools of net zero strategy for financial institutions. It elaborates the concepts on climate change, the measurement tool of greenhouse emissions, the low-carbon roadmap for financial institutions and the development of sustainable finance products related to climate change.
cilos: Understand the climate change risks and impacts.
Understand the financial institutions’ roles in net zero transition.
Master the practical skills of carbon measurement and climate reporting.
Develop the climate finance products.

FINA 5600.title: Real Estate Financing
FINA 5600.description: This course focuses on how real estate financing is undertaken and the key considerations for the borrower and the lender. This is achieved through a master case study which runs through the duration of the course and evolves as different aspects of real estate financing are discussed. The course will focus on the key steps in a transaction life-cycle and require participants to prepare basic cash-flow models, approval memos and negotiate term-sheets. The course also includes additional case studies around hedging and considerations around cross border real estate financings.
cilos: Describe the typical deal life-cycle of a financing transaction and how they differ for different type of clients, situations and products.
Undertake due diligence of a real estate transaction.
Write a credit approval memo for internal bank discussions.
Negotiate a term sheet.
Evaluate financing proposals from a borrower's perspective.
Identify the different financing situations and markets available to borrowers.

FINA 5670.title: Wealth Management
FINA 5670.description: With an introduction to the principles of wealth management and the financial planning process, this course progresses to cover various wealth management topics including consumption planning, investment planning and retirement planning. In particular, this course emphasizes on the provision of investment advisory services. It discusses client expectations and concerns including risk and other cognitive issues before applying the concepts and techniques to construct and manage investment portfolios for individual clients.
cilos: Apply personal profiling and risk profiling techniques to comprehend the unique situation and preferences of the client.
Prioritize goals for client given their unique situations and determine the feasibility of achieving these goals.
Construct personal financial statements and use ratios and other techniques to analyze the client's financial situation.
Construct optimal portfolios and make asset allocation decisions which match goals, risk tolerance and other client characteristics.
Clearly discuss and justify recommendations.

FINA 5680.title: Asia's Stock Markets
FINA 5680.description: This course is highly relevant to students interested to become macro-traders, portfolio managers, buy/sell-side analysts or work at a hedge fund, with a particular focus on Asia. The course will teach students the characteristics of the larger, liquid stock markets across Asia, from China and Hong Kong to Korea, Taiwan, India and ASEAN markets. Students will learn what drives these markets, what they have in common and how they behave.
cilos: Describe the differences in composition and architecture of the major Asian stock markets.
Explain “top-down” (macro) and “bottom-up” drivers of the major Asian stock markets.
Narrate recent dynamics in Asian equities and map these to a concrete investment plan.
Formulate an Asian stock market outlook.
Adapt an existing Asian market outlook to reflect changes in investment views.
Present a complex investment view in a concise and clear format.

FINA 5690.title: Family Office
FINA 5690.description: This course will provide students with a comprehensive and most up-to-date understanding of family office, as well as insiders’ view and practical aspects of family offices, especially Asian family offices. The course will address questions based on the extensive research and the latest case studies on family offices in Asia and around the world by the instructor.
cilos: Manage the wealth and achieve greater meaning of the wealth.
Understand fundamentals and wealth management role of family office.
Understand the impact investing and risk management of family office.
Understand the concepts of family trust and family governance.
Understand the family philanthropy and the family office development in China.

FINA 5700.title: Responsible Finance
FINA 5700.description: The aim of this course is to develop a deep understanding why the economic doctrine that the only social responsibility of corporations is to maximize profits does no longer work in today’s capital markets. The course provides theoretical and empirical findings that illustrate that financial decisions need to incorporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors to ensure long-term financial success of firms. The course also covers new trends, such as U.S. political polarization and the important role of China in establishing a global leadership role in green finance, which may impact how corporations are becoming more responsible.
cilos: Describe the fundamental driving forces of responsible finance.
Compare and contrast responsible finance and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) in relation to corporate objectives.
Explain how investors may engage with firms in effective manners.
Work in teams on cases to apply responsible finance theory to practice.
Utilize the tools and data sets used in evaluating ESG performance.
Propose a novel corporate project that grows the pie.
Broaden firm performance evaluation encompassing ESG methods.

FINA 5710.title: Green Finance and Capital Markets
FINA 5710.description: This course will cover sustainable and green finance with a focus in Hong Kong and China. Various green finance instruments, how green elements are factored in credit ratings and assessments, and the major external green review approaches are covered. This course will empower the students with the most updated knowledge, market trends and direct first-hand cases (rather than the public domain) in the green finance and capital market fields.
cilos: Compare and contrast various green finance and capital market products.
Describe and quantify the costs and benefits of green finance as it impacts credit ratings.
Explain and critique the green bond assessment process performed by credit rating agencies.
Apply the green certification approaches to the green bonds performed by certification service providers.

FINA 5720.title: Financial Advisory and Transaction Execution for M&A
FINA 5720.description: The course provides an understanding of executing mergers and acquisitions (M&A) transactions, with a specific focus on Asia and China. An in-depth exploration of M&A processes will help students to develop a working knowledge of how to execute an M&A deal - from identifying and analyzing target companies to conducting due diligence, securing financing, and closing the transaction. It will also cover constructing financial models and performing analyses throughout.
cilos: Analyze and identify various structures of M&A transactions for different types of situations.
Execute tools to complete M&A transactions and structure them in both public and private market environments.
Recognize how M&A transactions are financed, the implications of the funding mix, and how value is created in M&A through common analyses.
Plan M&A transactions from the perspective of financial investors, focusing on leveraged buyouts (LBOs).

FINA 5730.title: Sustainable Finance and Reporting Strategies in Hong Kong
FINA 5730.description: This course aims to develop students’ comprehensive knowledge, skills, and understanding of ESG, sustainable finance, and ESG reporting. Particular focus will be placed on the impact of ESG and sustainable finance on listed companies in Hong Kong. This course comprises both formal lectures and guest lectures to allow students to develop solid ESG and green finance knowledge, as well as understand the latest market and regulatory developments in Hong Kong.
cilos: List the latest ESG market and regulatory development.
Compare and contrast various sustainable finance products.
Develop a solid knowledge of green taxonomy and ESG reporting.

FINA 5740.title: Essential Financial Market Tools
FINA 5740.description: This course offers an advantage by empowering students with hands-on experience using some of the industry-leading financial tools. There are various certificates (e.g., Bloomberg Market Concepts, London Stock Exchange Group Finance Essentials) that students can earn during the course. Graded P or F.
cilos: Learn about the financial markets, Bloomberg data, news, and analytics via four core modules – Economic Indicators, Currencies, Fixed Income and Equities.
Access trusted, real-world market data, news and statistics that power the global financial community, so they can advance applied learning.
Perform financial analysis using Bloomberg terminal, London Stock Exchange group Workspace, Wind terminal and Morningstar Direct.

FINA 5750.title: Structured Product
FINA 5750.description: Structured products are one of the major products manufactured and distributed by investment banks given the increasing demand from institutional and individual investors. This course covers basic concepts of structured products, introduces popular products in the market (e.g., principal protected notes and equity-linked notes), and discusses the landscape of product manufacturing and distribution process. It focuses on applications rather than theory by illustrating real-world examples as well as their practical implementations in the industry.
cilos: Understand the nature of structured products.
Explain the key features, risks, and benefits of structured products.
Understand how structured products are manufactured and sold to clients.
Be familiar with popular structured products in the market and understand their pros and cons.
Analyze the typical structured products in the market.
Identify suitable products for potential clients given their risk appetite.
Make effective presentations to pitch potential clients.

FINA 5760.title: Navigating Capital Markets: A Practitioner's Guide to Capital Flows
FINA 5760.description: This course offers an in-depth exploration into the realm of global capital markets in practice. We will delve into the inner workings of financial markets, including primary and secondary markets, trading floors and market dynamics. Students will apply analytical skills to learn to identify opportunities across capital markets including synthesizing information, identifying capital uses and interpreting market sentiment and behavior. This course is designed to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and practical application. The focus is on equipping students with the insights needed to excel in the complex world of capital markets, providing a foundation for exploring more advanced subjects.
cilos: Explain the role of capital markets, from theory to practice.
Explain the flows of capital across market participants.
Explain various instruments used across the various asset classes.
Identify opportunities in the movement of capital.
Understand the mechanics and role of capital markets in managing flows between stakeholders.
Identify the different roles available and how a potential career in capital markets may develop.

FINA 5770.title: Strategic Corporate Financing: IPOs, Debt, and Private Equity Solutions
FINA 5770.description: This course provides a practical understanding of corporate financing solutions from issuers' and investors' perspectives. Public market equity funding is explored, focusing on initial public offerings (IPOs) and their impact on companies and stakeholders. Debt as a funding source is examined, with key debt instruments analyzed in the context of leveraged buyouts. Private market equity financing is covered, using early-stage and pre-IPO companies as examples. Hands-on elements include constructing Excel models and conducting analyses throughout the course.
cilos: Recognize how to structure and execute capital raising transactions for businesses at various stages of their life cycles.
Evaluate how companies are valued in the context of such transactions.
Develop deeper understanding of the impact of various forms of capital raising on both the company (or the issuer) and the investor.
Execute their knowledge of corporate finance and apply it to real-world situations and transactions.

FINA 5780.title: Climate Finance and Energy Transition
FINA 5780.description: This course examines how climate and transition finance can help avert climate change and accelerate the shift to clean energy. It focuses on financial instruments, market mechanisms, and policy frameworks that support decarbonization, carbon pricing, and emissions reduction. Key topics include carbon markets, renewable and climate tech investments, nature-based solutions, and corporate finance for the energy transition.
cilos: Explain possible financial solutions to climate change and its social and economic contexts using finance and management knowledge and concepts.
Evaluate financial sector impacts on climate solutions and the energy transition with evidence-based approaches.
Appropriately communicate the role of the financial industry in climate change and transition finance including positive and negative examples of climate finance to different stakeholders.
Develop strategies and solutions to promote effective financial tools to mitigate climate change and transition away from fossil fuels.

FINA 5840.title: Financial Modeling
FINA 5840.description: This is a course about financial modeling.  The goal is to make financial models that produce useful answers to economic questions.  Selected topics which lend themselves to financial modeling will be covered, such as (but not limited to) loan amortization schedules; valuation and private equity; equity derivatives; mutual fund performance and style analysis; fixed income derivatives, and optimal portfolio selection.
cilos: Use Excel formulas, functions and commands in finance-related applications.
Implement in spreadsheet format concepts from finance theory, with emphasis on portfolio choice and valuation of derivatives and fixed income securities.
Gain hands-on experience in designing finance models.
Critically evaluate the strengths and limitations of the output of various financial models in principle, and those implemented in a spreadsheet in particular.

FINA 5870.title: Big Data in Finance
FINA 5870.description: This course introduces students to the concepts of big data and machine learning with a special focus on how these tools can be applied in a financial context. During the course students will learn Python and how it can be used to build and estimate some of the most commonly used machine learning models such as regression, clustering and classification. Students will also learn the basics of cloud computing and how the cloud can be employed to quickly estimate complex models with very large data sets.
FINA 5870.prerequisite: ISOM 5510 OR ISOM 5520 (prior to 2022-23) OR FINA 5240 OR FINA 5250
cilos: Define what big data is and how it relates to finance.
Work with Python.
Use Python to produce basic statistics and visualize data.
Describe the basic mathematical rationale for state-of-the-art machine learning models.
Use Python to estimate machine learning models on real-world data.
Explain how cloud computing technologies can be employed to facilitate quick estimation of complex.

FINA 6900-6910.title: Special Topics
FINA 6900-6910.description: Current developments in finance. Topics selected by the instructor.
cilos: Apply the financial knowledge to real-world investment management and securities valuation.
Develop sophisticated financial models to support decision making.
Propose asset/risk-management solutions that maximize firm value.

FINA 6920.title: Finance Practicum
FINA 6920.description: This course is a unique opportunity for students in the MSc in Finance program to gain practical experience and apply their knowledge in a professional setting. By completing the Practicum, students will be equipped with practical experience, enhanced professional skills, and a deeper understanding of the complexities and challenges in the financial industry. Graded P or F.
cilos: Apply theoretical knowledge and skills acquired throughout the program to real-world scenarios in the financial industry.
Demonstrate effective problem-solving, critical thinking, and communication skills in a professional setting.
Understand the complexities and challenges faced in the financial industry and develop strategies to address them.
Reflect on their internship experiences and identify areas of personal and professional growth.
Integrate academic knowledge with practical experiences in real scenarios in the financial industry.

FINA 6970.title: Independent Study
FINA 6970.description: Study of selected financial issues under the supervision of a faculty member. (Special permission from the Associate Dean is required for MBA students to take this course.)
cilos: Have up-to-date and in-depth knowledge of finance, leading to independent substantive scholarly research.

FINA 6990.title: MPhil Thesis Research
FINA 6990.description: Master's thesis research supervised by a faculty member.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of core business functions.

FINA 7900.title: Doctoral Seminar
FINA 7900.description: Current research topics in corporate finance, investments, financial markets and institutions, derivative securities, and empirical research in financial economics.
cilos: Present their discipline knowledge clearly to laymen.

FINA 7910.title: Doctoral Seminar: Theoretical Corporate Finance
FINA 7910.description: The course will emphasize theoretical frameworks that underlie some of the important ideas in modern corporate finance.  Topics covered will be (i) Financial Contracting, (ii) Capital Structure and Corporate Strategy , (iii) Agency Problems, Investment Distortions, and Discipline, (iv) Information Asymmetry and Financing,(v) Corporate Governance. The theory will be motivated by and connected to empirical facts, although we will not go into details of empirical papers on the topics. An important goal is to help students learn how to write down a basic model to capture an idea.

FINA 7920.title: Doctoral Seminar: Theoretical Asset Pricing
FINA 7920.description: This course offers an introduction to asset pricing. The intention of the course is to provide a basis in the neoclassical theory of finance that underlies the other PhD-level finance courses. It uses the theory of choice under uncertainty to develop classical asset pricing theory in discrete time. The two main parts of the course focus on static asset pricing models and dynamic asset pricing models with a representative agent. Throughout, the course discusses several empirical puzzles and theories that have been developed to try to solve them.

FINA 7930.title: Doctoral Seminar: Empirical Corporate Finance
FINA 7930.description: This course covers major topics in empirical corporate finance. A large part of this course is devoted to examining research questions in capital structure, corporate investments, and corporate governance. The focus is on the more recent literature in these broad areas of corporate finance. The goal of the course is to help students get ready for doing their own research.

FINA 7940.title: Doctoral Seminar: Empirical Asset Pricing
FINA 7940.description: Part one of the course covers various issues and empirical methods in asset pricing studies. Empirical issues regarding time-series properties of asset prices are discussed first, followed by the cross-sectional implications of asset pricing models. Applications in bond, currency, and futures markets will also be discussed. Part two of the course is designed to provide students with the exposure to empirical finance, with the focus on investment and behavioral finance.

FINA 7980.title: Finance Workshops
FINA 7980.description: Papers presented by faculty, students and visitors. Mandatory for all PhD students.  May be repeated for credit. Graded P or F.
cilos: Have up-to-date and in-depth knowledge of finance, leading to independent substantive scholarly research.

FINA 7990.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
FINA 7990.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research.  A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass.  No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Apply their specialized knowledge to solve related business problems in an innovative fashion.
